Definition: from G1909 and G5087; to impose (in a friendly or hostile sense):--add unto, lade, lay upon, put (up) on, set on (up), + surname, X wound.
BiblicalUsage: Epitíthēmi means to lay upon — to put a hand, a name, or a burden on something. The apostles lay hands on the seven, and on new believers who receive the Spirit; Jesus lays His hands on children and blesses them. The laying on of hands is the visible sign of blessing and commissioning.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe epitíthēmi is a word for how blessing passes from person to person: by touch, in the open, before witnesses. I hold that the laying on of hands still matters, because God still works through His people's hands.
RelatedEvents: Martyrdom of Stephen; Philip Preaches in Samaria
